clue.text: Plan to recycle liqueur

parts.note: a chart is a plan or map
to reuse something is to recycle it

explanation.surface: A scheme to put old bottles of liqueur back into use.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartreuse is a green or yellow herbal liqueur made by Carthusian monks.

clue.text: Will him to succeed

parts.note: reads as urging someone on, but describes the person a legal will names to inherit

explanation.surface: Willing someone on to success.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament names the beneficiary who will take over an estate or title.

clue.text: Come to life again and get out of bed

explanation.surface: Reviving and rising in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebel or revolt is one sense of the phrase, here stretched to coming back to life; it also means rising from sleep.

clue.text: Managed to fire rifle

parts.note: ran a business means managed it
to sack someone is to dismiss or fire them

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded in firing a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' looks like a gun, but here it is the verb meaning to search and plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle through a place is to search it thoroughly and steal from it.

clue.text: Prompt action?

parts.note: reads as a call for speed, but describes an impulse that prompts someone to act

explanation.surface: A request for swift action.
explanation.definitionFit: An impulse or strong desire is what spurs someone into doing something.

clue.text: Beg for something nice to follow in French

indicators.note: says the nice thing comes after the French word

parts.note: en is French for in
a treat is something nice

explanation.surface: Pleading for a sweet in a French lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech or plead with someone is to beg them.

clue.text: There may be plenty of jumpers at this trading centre

definitions.text: There may be plenty of jumpers at this trading centre

parts.words: There may be plenty of jumpers at this trading centre
parts.note: jumpers suggests sweaters on a market stall, but also means the hopping insects the name refers to

explanation.surface: A market stall piled high with knitted sweaters.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a sweater; the pun is on fleas as jumpers.
explanation.definitionFit: A street market selling second-hand goods is named after the jumping insects.

clue.text: Anaemic pet treated and set free

indicators.note: treated suggests a vet's care, signalling the letters are worked on and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sickly pet is given veterinary care and then released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges the ten letters of ANAEMIC and PET.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate someone from bondage is to set them free.

clue.text: Fifty stick around, looking far from pleased

indicators.note: the stick goes around the fifty

parts.note: gum is a glue, something used to stick
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone told to stay put looks sulky.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone glum is gloomy and dejected, plainly unhappy.

clue.text: Start of play

parts.note: reads as the opening of a game, but means the opening performance of a stage production

explanation.surface: The beginning of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The premiere evening of a theatrical run is the beginning of a drama's life.

clue.text: Keep your thanks in check

indicators.note: places the thanks inside the check

parts.note: to rein is to check or restrain
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: Holding back your gratitude.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold on to something is to keep it.

clue.text: His guilt is a possibility

parts.note: describes a person whom police think may have committed a crime

explanation.surface: A man may be guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: A person under suspicion is one whose culpability is possible but unproven.

clue.text: Turn and jump in amazement

parts.note: a spell is a turn or stint
a bound is a leap or jump

explanation.surface: Someone spins and leaps in astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Being entranced or enthralled is being held in wonder.

clue.text: He may get one person LBW

definitions.text: He may get one person LBW

parts.words: He may get one person LBW
parts.note: LBW is the cricket dismissal leg before wicket; a slow bowler who turns the ball often traps batsmen this way

explanation.surface: A cricketer who dismisses a batsman leg before wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, LBW (leg before wicket) is a way a batsman is given out; the clue points to a slow, turning bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow bowler who makes the ball turn off the pitch can trap a batsman leg before wicket.

clue.text: Start to raise issue at lawcourt

definitions.text: Start to raise issue at lawcourt

parts.words: Start to raise issue at lawcourt
parts.note: describes the hearing in which a dispute is brought before a court

explanation.surface: Someone begins to bring a matter before the courts.
explanation.definitionFit: A court hearing examines evidence to decide a case.

clue.text: Drink in the fresh air next to the tents

indicators.note: places the tents beside the rearranged air

parts.note: a camp is a group of tents

indicators.note: fresh suggests something new, so the letters of air are made anew

explanation.surface: Having a drink outdoors beside the campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the fresh air' reads as the setting, but 'fresh' is the anagram signal working on the word air.
explanation.definitionFit: Campari is an Italian bitter aperitif.

clue.text: Names grounds for development at a hearing

indicators.note: says the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: sites are plots of ground for building

explanation.surface: A court hearing names the reasons for a building project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at a hearing' signals a sound-alike: SITES is said the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To mention or quote someone as an authority is to name them.

clue.text: Soldier in full gear creeps around at night

indicators.note: puts the soldier inside the gear

parts.note: kit is a full set of equipment
RA, the Royal Artillery, gives a gunner or soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier in combat dress moves stealthily on a night patrol.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: the krait is a nocturnal venomous snake of Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: This venomous Asian snake is nocturnal, hunting by slithering about after dark.

clue.text: Get out of this!'

parts.note: reads as a cry of disbelief, but is an instruction pointing to the door one leaves by

explanation.surface: An exclamation of disbelief.
explanation.definitionFit: A way out is the door through which you leave.

clue.text: A bird others turn to?

indicators.note: says the other birds' name is turned round

parts.note: auks are other seabirds, the family the clue points to

explanation.surface: A bird others look to for guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn to' reads backwards the seabirds AUKS.
explanation.definitionFit: The skua is a predatory seabird that robs gulls of their food.

clue.text: Fed up with dates having to be re-arranged

indicators.note: plainly says the letters of the dates are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tired of having appointments rescheduled.
explanation.definitionFit: Having eaten one's fill means being satisfied, full up.

clue.text: Spit in the sea

parts.note: reads as rude behaviour at the beach, but spit here is a narrow ridge of land jutting into water

explanation.surface: Someone spitting into the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge of sand built up by currents in shallow water forms a coastal spit.

clue.text: Security is lifted in the store

indicators.note: places the turned word inside the store

parts.note: a depot is a storehouse

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the word is reads upwards

explanation.surface: Something valuable has been stolen from a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' suggests theft from the shop, but in a down clue it means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum paid as a guarantee against damage is security.

clue.text: Politician makes a defamatory statement about an artist

indicators.note: the statement goes around the artist

parts.note: a libel is a published defamatory statement
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A politician libels a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Liberal Party is a politician.

clue.text: Let's eat out in America

indicators.note: out suggests disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An invitation to dine out while visiting the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of LET'S EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is a city in Washington State, so it lies in the United States.

clue.text: Fear of finishing last by mistake

indicators.note: finishing points to the final letter of the word last

parts.note: an error is a mistake

explanation.surface: Dread of coming last through a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishing' takes the final letter of 'last', T.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme fright or dread is fear.

clue.text: Go-ahead place of duty for nurse

explanation.surface: A hospital nurse is told to proceed to the ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward is the first sense, as in a cry to advance; a nurse working is on a ward.

clue.text: Advertise an electrical fitting

explanation.surface: Promoting a socket for the mains.
explanation.definitionFit: To promote a product is to advertise it; the three-pin connector on a cable is an electrical fitting.

clue.text: Side turning Caesar was warned about

indicators.note: turning suggests the letters of side are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A side road Caesar was told to avoid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges SIDE. A soothsayer told Julius Caesar to beware the Ides of March.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar was told to beware the fifteenth of March, the day he was assassinated.

clue.text: Protection on landing for party backing American commerce

indicators.note: the party name is read in reverse

parts.note: Lab is short for the Labour Party
trade is commerce

explanation.surface: An aircraft landing protected by a party that supports US trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses LAB to BAL. 'landing' means the floor at the top of stairs, not a plane touching down.
explanation.definitionFit: A railing with its supporting posts guards the edge of a staircase landing.

clue.text: Ones, perhaps, who vote against

indicators.note: perhaps signals the word Ones could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: People who might cast votes against a motion.
explanation.definitionFit: In a parliamentary division, the votes against are counted as the opposite of the ayes.

clue.text: Correct attire for Army manoeuvre

parts.note: right means correct
dress is attire

explanation.surface: The proper uniform for a military exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: The drill command for soldiers to align themselves with the man on the right is a parade-ground movement.
